environment.description: Application deployed on EKS (Kubernetes 1.28) with a Pod Security Standard of 'restricted' enforced at namespace level via PodSecurity admission controller. The pod spec includes a custom seccomp profile loaded via the node's /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/strict-noexec.json which allows only: read, write, open, openat, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, socket, connect, sendto, recvfrom, bind, listen, accept, clone, exit_group, futex, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, getpid, getuid, geteuid, getgid, getegid, fcntl, lseek, stat, lstat, poll, nanosleep, clock_gettime — notably EXCLUDES execve, execveat, fork, vfork, and clone with CLONE_THREAD unset. Additionally, the container's root filesystem is mounted read-only (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true) with only an emptyDir volume at /tmp/uploads that has the 'noexec' mount option via a projected volume with medium: Memory. The Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricts egress to only the cluster DNS (kube-dns on port 53/UDP) and the application's own service port.
